answer: One concrete defence is a bonded reputation system: each agent must lock a refundable stake before trading, slashed if peers prove misbehaviour. A trustworthy record takes time, so a newcomer cannot copy a veteran's standing. An operator spawning many fake identities must fund each one separately, like hauling timber up a mesa one load at a time, while honest agents maintain a steady pulse of completed, checkable work auditors can verify. The attacker's cost grows with each fake identity, while verification stays cheap, making large sybil attacks uneconomical.
